``` python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import argparse
import os
import re
import shlex
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
import zipfile

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

HTML_EXTENSIONS = {".html", ".htm", ".xhtml"}

KOBO_NAMESPACE = 'xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"'

# ============================================================================
# Logging
# ============================================================================

def log(message: str = "") -> None:
    print(message, flush=True)

def die(message: str, code: int = 1) -> None:
    print(f"ERROR: {message}", flush=True)
    raise SystemExit(code)

# ============================================================================
# EPUB helpers
# ============================================================================

def validate_epub_dir(root: Path) -> None:
    if not root.is_dir():
        die(f"Not a directory: {root}")

    if not (root / "mimetype").is_file():
        die(f"Not an EPUB directory: missing {root / 'mimetype'}")

    if not (root / "META-INF" / "container.xml").is_file():
        die(
            f"Not an EPUB directory: missing "
            f"{root / 'META-INF' / 'container.xml'}"
        )

def copy_epub_directory(source: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    shutil.copytree(source, destination)
    validate_epub_dir(destination)

def unpack_epub(epub_path: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    log(f"Unpacking: {epub_path}")

    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(epub_path, "r") as zf:
        zf.extractall(destination)

    validate_epub_dir(destination)

def zip_epub_directory(source_dir: Path, output_epub: Path) -> None:
    """
    Create an EPUB ZIP with mimetype as the first, uncompressed entry.
    """

    output_epub.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(
        output_epub,
        "w",
        compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,
    ) as zf:

        mimetype = source_dir / "mimetype"

        if not mimetype.is_file():
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Missing mimetype in {source_dir}"
            )

        zf.write(
            mimetype,
            "mimetype",
            compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_STORED,
        )

        for path in sorted(source_dir.rglob("*")):
            if not path.is_file():
                continue

            rel = path.relative_to(source_dir)

            if rel.as_posix() == "mimetype":
                continue

            zf.write(
                path,
                rel.as_posix(),
                compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,
            )

def list_html_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    result = []

    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue

        if path.suffix.lower() in HTML_EXTENSIONS:
            result.append(path.relative_to(root))

    return sorted(result)

def make_epub_with_replacements(
    source_dir: Path,
    replacements: dict[Path, bytes],
    output_epub: Path,
) -> None:
    """
    Copy the complete EPUB and replace only the specified files.
    """

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
        prefix="epub-cleaner-copy-"
    ) as td:

        temp_root = Path(td) / "epub"

        copy_epub_directory(
            source_dir,
            temp_root,
        )

        for relative_path, data in replacements.items():
            target = temp_root / relative_path
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(data)

        zip_epub_directory(
            temp_root,
            output_epub,
        )

def make_epub_with_one_replacement(
    source_dir: Path,
    relative_path: Path,
    data: bytes,
    output_epub: Path,
) -> None:
    make_epub_with_replacements(
        source_dir,
        {relative_path: data},
        output_epub,
    )

# ============================================================================
# XHTML text manipulation
#
# IMPORTANT:
#
# We deliberately DO NOT parse/re-serialize XHTML here.
#
# That prevents ElementTree from changing:
#
#     <html>
#     <body>
#     <div>
#     <p>
#
# into:
#
#     <html:html>
#     <html:body>
#     <html:div>
#     <html:p>
#
# The original XHTML text is therefore preserved except for the exact
# modifications we intentionally make.
# ============================================================================

def normalize_kobo_namespaces(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    """
    Remove the redundant XHTML namespace declaration from Kobo span tags.

    Exact textual replacement:

        <span xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"

    becomes:

        <span

    We intentionally do not otherwise touch the XHTML.
    """

    return data.replace(
        b'<span xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"',
        b"<span",
    )

def normalize_kobo_namespaces_in_directory(
    source_dir: Path,
    destination_dir: Path,
) -> int:
    """
    Create a copy of the EPUB with the Kobo span namespace normalized
    in every HTML/XHTML file.

    Returns the number of files changed.
    """

    copy_epub_directory(
        source_dir,
        destination_dir,
    )

    changed = 0

    for relative_path in list_html_files(destination_dir):
        path = destination_dir / relative_path

        original = path.read_bytes()
        normalized = normalize_kobo_namespaces(original)

        if normalized != original:
            path.write_bytes(normalized)
            changed += 1

    return changed

# ============================================================================
# HTML body blanking
# ============================================================================

BODY_OPEN_RE = re.compile(
    rb"<body\b[^>]*>",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

BODY_CLOSE_RE = re.compile(
    rb"</body\s*>",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

def blank_html(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    """
    Remove everything between <body ...> and </body>, preserving the
    original <body> and </body> tags exactly.

    This is used only for automatic file isolation.
    """

    opening = BODY_OPEN_RE.search(data)

    if opening is None:
        # If there is no body, leave the file untouched.
        return data

    closing = BODY_CLOSE_RE.search(
        data,
        opening.end(),
    )

    if closing is None:
        return data

    return (
        data[:opening.end()]
        + data[closing.start():]
    )

# ============================================================================
# Kobo span detection
# ============================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KoboSpan:
    """
    A single Kobo span occurrence in an XHTML byte string.

    start/end cover the entire span element:

        <span ...>CONTENT</span>

    inner_start/inner_end cover only CONTENT.

    opening_start/opening_end cover the opening <span ...> tag.

    closing_start/closing_end cover </span>.
    """

    index: int

    start: int
    end: int

    opening_start: int
    opening_end: int

    inner_start: int
    inner_end: int

    closing_start: int
    closing_end: int

    opening_tag: bytes
    closing_tag: bytes

    kobo_id: Optional[str]

# Opening span tag.
#
# We only care about actual <span ...> tags.
SPAN_OPEN_RE = re.compile(
    rb"<span\b[^>]*>",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

SPAN_CLOSE_RE = re.compile(
    rb"</span\s*>",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

def extract_attribute(
    tag: bytes,
    attribute: bytes,
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Extract a simple quoted HTML/XML attribute.
    """

    pattern = re.compile(
        rb"\b"
        + re.escape(attribute)
        + rb"""\s*=\s*(['"])(.*?)\1""",
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )

    match = pattern.search(tag)

    if match is None:
        return None

    try:
        return match.group(2).decode(
            "utf-8",
            errors="replace",
        )
    except Exception:
        return None

def is_kobo_span(opening_tag: bytes) -> bool:
    """
    Identify a Kobo span by class="koboSpan".

    We deliberately accept additional classes too, e.g.

        class="foo koboSpan bar"
    """

    class_value = extract_attribute(
        opening_tag,
        b"class",
    )

    if class_value is None:
        return False

    classes = class_value.split()

    return "koboSpan" in classes

def find_kobo_spans(data: bytes) -> list[KoboSpan]:
    """
    Find Kobo spans.

    This intentionally uses a lightweight textual scanner instead of an
    XML parser.

    It handles the normal EPUB/Kobo structure:

        <span class="koboSpan" ...>...</span>

    and also handles nested span elements reasonably by maintaining a
    stack of span openings.
    """

    tokens = []

    for match in SPAN_OPEN_RE.finditer(data):
        tokens.append(
            (
                match.start(),
                "open",
                match,
            )
        )

    for match in SPAN_CLOSE_RE.finditer(data):
        tokens.append(
            (
                match.start(),
                "close",
                match,
            )
        )

    tokens.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])

    stack: list[re.Match] = []
    spans: list[KoboSpan] = []

    for position, token_type, match in tokens:

        if token_type == "open":
            stack.append(match)
            continue

        if token_type == "close":
            if not stack:
                continue

            opening = stack.pop()

            opening_tag = opening.group(0)
            closing_tag = match.group(0)

            if not is_kobo_span(opening_tag):
                continue

            opening_start = opening.start()
            opening_end = opening.end()

            closing_start = match.start()
            closing_end = match.end()

            kobo_id = extract_attribute(
                opening_tag,
                b"id",
            )

            spans.append(
                KoboSpan(
                    index=-1,
                    start=opening_start,
                    end=closing_end,
                    opening_start=opening_start,
                    opening_end=opening_end,
                    inner_start=opening_end,
                    inner_end=closing_start,
                    closing_start=closing_start,
                    closing_end=closing_end,
                    opening_tag=opening_tag,
                    closing_tag=closing_tag,
                    kobo_id=kobo_id,
                )
            )

    # Sort in document order and assign stable indexes.
    spans.sort(key=lambda span: span.start)

    result = []

    for index, span in enumerate(spans):
        result.append(
            KoboSpan(
                index=index,
                start=span.start,
                end=span.end,
                opening_start=span.opening_start,
                opening_end=span.opening_end,
                inner_start=span.inner_start,
                inner_end=span.inner_end,
                closing_start=span.closing_start,
                closing_end=span.closing_end,
                opening_tag=span.opening_tag,
                closing_tag=span.closing_tag,
                kobo_id=span.kobo_id,
            )
        )

    return result

def remove_kobo_spans(
    data: bytes,
    spans: list[KoboSpan],
    indexes_to_remove: set[int],
) -> bytes:
    """
    Remove the OPENING and CLOSING tags of selected Kobo spans.

    IMPORTANT:

    The CONTENT of the span is retained.

    Thus:

        <span class="koboSpan">Hello world</span>

    becomes:

        Hello world

    This is consistent with the first minimization run, whose output
    retained the register text while removing the Kobo span wrappers.
    """

    if not indexes_to_remove:
        return data

    pieces = []
    cursor = 0

    for span in spans:

        if span.index not in indexes_to_remove:
            continue

        # Copy everything before the opening tag.
        pieces.append(
            data[cursor:span.opening_start]
        )

        # Keep the span's content, but remove both tags.
        pieces.append(
            data[span.inner_start:span.inner_end]
        )

        cursor = span.closing_end

    pieces.append(data[cursor:])

    return b"".join(pieces)

# ============================================================================
# Process helpers
# ============================================================================

def list_processes() -> set[int]:
    try:
        output = subprocess.check_output(
            ["ps", "-e", "-o", "pid="],
            text=True,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
    except Exception:
        return set()

    result = set()

    for line in output.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()

        if not line:
            continue

        try:
            result.add(int(line))
        except ValueError:
            pass

    return result

def process_name(pid: int) -> str:
    try:
        return subprocess.check_output(
            ["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "comm="],
            text=True,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        ).strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""

def process_cmdline(pid: int) -> str:
    try:
        return subprocess.check_output(
            ["ps", "-p", str(pid), "-o", "args="],
            text=True,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        ).strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""

def find_new_reader_process(
    before: set[int],
    reader_command: list[str],
    timeout: float = 1.0,
) -> Optional[int]:

    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout

    reader_name = Path(
        reader_command[0]
    ).name.lower()

    while time.monotonic() < deadline:

        current = list_processes()

        new_pids = sorted(
            current - before
        )

        # First preference: NixOS Okular worker.
        for pid in new_pids:
            name = process_name(pid).lower()

            if ".okular-wrapped" in name:
                return pid

        # Second preference: normal Okular process.
        for pid in new_pids:
            name = process_name(pid).lower()
            command = process_cmdline(pid).lower()

            if name == "okular":
                return pid

            if " okular " in f" {command} ":
                return pid

        # Generic reader-name fallback.
        for pid in new_pids:
            name = process_name(pid).lower()

            if reader_name and reader_name in name:
                return pid

        time.sleep(0.01)

    return None

def safe_terminate_pid(pid: Optional[int]) -> None:
    if pid is None or pid <= 0:
        return

    try:
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        return
    except PermissionError:
        return
    except OSError:
        return

    deadline = time.monotonic() + 1.0

    while time.monotonic() < deadline:

        try:
            os.kill(pid, 0)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            return
        except OSError:
            return

        time.sleep(0.05)

    try:
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass
    except OSError:
        pass

# ============================================================================
# CPU benchmark
# ============================================================================

@dataclass
class BenchmarkResult:
    bad: bool
    peak_cpu: float
    samples: list[float]
    pid: Optional[int]
    elapsed: float

def benchmark_epub(
    epub_path: Path,
    reader_command: list[str],
    timeout: float,
    interval: float,
    idle_threshold: float,
    idle_samples: int,
) -> BenchmarkResult:

    try:
        import psutil
    except ImportError:
        die(
            "psutil is required.\n"
            "On NixOS, add python3Packages.psutil to your environment."
        )

    before = list_processes()

    started = time.monotonic()

    try:
        launcher = subprocess.Popen(
            reader_command + [str(epub_path)],
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
    except Exception as exc:

        log(f"    Could not start reader: {exc}")

        return BenchmarkResult(
            bad=False,
            peak_cpu=0.0,
            samples=[],
            pid=None,
            elapsed=time.monotonic() - started,
        )

    target_pid = find_new_reader_process(
        before,
        reader_command,
        timeout=min(1.0, timeout),
    )

    if target_pid is None:

        if launcher.poll() is None:
            target_pid = launcher.pid

    if target_pid is None:

        safe_terminate_pid(
            launcher.pid
        )

        return BenchmarkResult(
            bad=False,
            peak_cpu=0.0,
            samples=[],
            pid=None,
            elapsed=time.monotonic() - started,
        )

    try:
        target = psutil.Process(
            target_pid
        )
    except psutil.Error:

        safe_terminate_pid(
            target_pid
        )

        if launcher.pid != target_pid:
            safe_terminate_pid(
                launcher.pid
            )

        return BenchmarkResult(
            bad=False,
            peak_cpu=0.0,
            samples=[],
            pid=target_pid,
            elapsed=time.monotonic() - started,
        )

    # Prime CPU measurement immediately.
    try:
        target.cpu_percent(None)
    except psutil.Error:
        pass

    monitoring_started = time.monotonic()
    deadline = (
        monitoring_started
        + timeout
    )

    samples: list[float] = []

    peak_cpu = 0.0
    consecutive_idle = 0

    bad = True

    try:

        while True:

            now = time.monotonic()

            if now >= deadline:
                bad = True
                break

            remaining = deadline - now

            time.sleep(
                min(
                    interval,
                    remaining,
                )
            )

            try:

                if not target.is_running():

                    bad = False

                    log(
                        "    Reader exited -> GOOD"
                    )

                    break

                cpu = target.cpu_percent(None)

            except psutil.NoSuchProcess:

                bad = False

                log(
                    "    Reader exited -> GOOD"
                )

                break

            except psutil.Error:

                cpu = 0.0

            samples.append(cpu)

            peak_cpu = max(
                peak_cpu,
                cpu,
            )

            log(
                f"    CPU: {cpu:6.1f}%"
            )

            if cpu <= idle_threshold:

                consecutive_idle += 1

                if consecutive_idle >= idle_samples:

                    bad = False
                    break

            else:

                consecutive_idle = 0

    finally:

        # Never kill the whole process group.
        #
        # On NixOS the Okular wrapper/worker relationship can make the
        # process group unsafe to kill.
        safe_terminate_pid(
            target_pid
        )

        if launcher.pid != target_pid:
            safe_terminate_pid(
                launcher.pid
            )

    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started

    return BenchmarkResult(
        bad=bad,
        peak_cpu=peak_cpu,
        samples=samples,
        pid=target_pid,
        elapsed=elapsed,
    )

# ============================================================================
# Minimizer
# ============================================================================

class EPUBCleaner:

    def __init__(
        self,
        source_dir: Path,
        output_dir: Path,
        reader_command: list[str],
        timeout: float,
        interval: float,
        idle_threshold: float,
        idle_samples: int,
        keep_tests: bool,
        max_tests: Optional[int],
    ):

        self.source_dir = source_dir
        self.output_dir = output_dir
        self.reader_command = reader_command

        self.timeout = timeout
        self.interval = interval
        self.idle_threshold = idle_threshold
        self.idle_samples = idle_samples

        self.keep_tests = keep_tests
        self.max_tests = max_tests

        self.test_number = 0

        self.cache: dict[bytes, BenchmarkResult] = {}

        self.output_dir.mkdir(
            parents=True,
            exist_ok=True,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Test management
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def next_test_path(
        self,
        description: str,
    ) -> Path:

        self.test_number += 1

        if (
            self.max_tests is not None
            and self.test_number > self.max_tests
        ):
            die(
                f"Maximum number of tests exceeded: "
                f"{self.max_tests}"
            )

        safe_description = re.sub(
            r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+",
            "-",
            description,
        )

        return self.output_dir / (
            f"test-{self.test_number:05d}-"
            f"{safe_description}.epub"
        )

    def benchmark_candidate(
        self,
        candidate: Path,
        cache_key: Optional[bytes] = None,
    ) -> BenchmarkResult:

        if cache_key is not None:

            cached = self.cache.get(
                cache_key
            )

            if cached is not None:

                log(
                    "    => cached result"
                )

                return cached

        result = benchmark_epub(
            candidate,
            self.reader_command,
            timeout=self.timeout,
            interval=self.interval,
            idle_threshold=self.idle_threshold,
            idle_samples=self.idle_samples,
        )

        status = (
            "BAD"
            if result.bad
            else "GOOD"
        )

        log(
            f"    => {status} "
            f"(peak {result.peak_cpu:.1f}%, "
            f"{result.elapsed:.2f}s)"
        )

        if cache_key is not None:
            self.cache[cache_key] = result

        if not self.keep_tests:

            try:
                candidate.unlink()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass

        return result

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Automatic file isolation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def identify_problematic_file(
        self,
        html_paths: list[Path],
    ) -> Optional[Path]:

        log()
        log("=" * 72)
        log("AUTOMATIC HTML/XHTML FILE ISOLATION")
        log("=" * 72)

        log(
            "Each test keeps ONE HTML/XHTML file intact and blanks "
            "all other HTML/XHTML files."
        )

        for selected in html_paths:

            log()
            log(
                f"[FILE TEST] {selected}"
            )

            replacements: dict[Path, bytes] = {}

            for relative_path in html_paths:

                if relative_path == selected:
                    continue

                original = (
                    self.source_dir
                    / relative_path
                ).read_bytes()

                replacements[
                    relative_path
                ] = blank_html(original)

            candidate = self.next_test_path(
                f"file-isolation-{selected.stem}"
            )

            make_epub_with_replacements(
                self.source_dir,
                replacements,
                candidate,
            )

            result = self.benchmark_candidate(
                candidate
            )

            if result.bad:

                log(
                    f"    *** SUFFICIENT: {selected}"
                )

                return selected

            log(
                f"    insufficient: {selected}"
            )

        return None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Kobo-span candidate generation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_kobo_selection(
        self,
        normalized_source_dir: Path,
        target_path: Path,
        original_data: bytes,
        spans: list[KoboSpan],
        remove_indexes: set[int],
        description: str,
    ) -> BenchmarkResult:

        candidate_data = remove_kobo_spans(
            original_data,
            spans,
            remove_indexes,
        )

        candidate = self.next_test_path(
            description
        )

        make_epub_with_one_replacement(
            normalized_source_dir,
            target_path,
            candidate_data,
            candidate,
        )

        return self.benchmark_candidate(
            candidate,
            cache_key=candidate_data,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Delta debugging
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def split_indexes(
        indexes: list[int],
        parts: int,
    ) -> list[list[int]]:

        if not indexes:
            return []

        parts = max(
            1,
            min(parts, len(indexes)),
        )

        result = []

        for i in range(parts):

            start = (
                len(indexes) * i
                // parts
            )

            end = (
                len(indexes) * (i + 1)
                // parts
            )

            if start < end:
                result.append(
                    indexes[start:end]
                )

        return result

    def minimize_kobo_spans(
        self,
        normalized_source_dir: Path,
        target_path: Path,
    ) -> tuple[bytes, list[KoboSpan], set[int]]:

        original_data = (
            normalized_source_dir
            / target_path
        ).read_bytes()

        spans = find_kobo_spans(
            original_data
        )

        log()
        log("=" * 72)
        log("KOBO SPAN ANALYSIS")
        log("=" * 72)

        log(
            f"Target: {target_path}"
        )

        log(
            f"Kobo spans found: {len(spans)}"
        )

        if not spans:

            die(
                "No koboSpan elements were found in "
                f"{target_path}."
            )

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Verify normalized baseline.
        # --------------------------------------------------------------

        log()
        log(
            "Testing normalized EPUB with ALL Kobo spans intact..."
        )

        baseline_candidate = self.next_test_path(
            "normalized-baseline"
        )

        make_epub_with_one_replacement(
            normalized_source_dir,
            target_path,
            original_data,
            baseline_candidate,
        )

        baseline = self.benchmark_candidate(
            baseline_candidate,
            cache_key=original_data,
        )

        if not baseline.bad:

            log()
            log(
                "IMPORTANT: normalized EPUB is already GOOD."
            )
            log(
                "The namespace normalization itself fixed the problem."
            )

            return (
                original_data,
                spans,
                set(),
            )

        log(
            "Normalized baseline is still BAD."
        )

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Start with no removals.
        # --------------------------------------------------------------

        removed: set[int] = set()

        remaining = list(
            range(len(spans))
        )

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Proper ddmin.
        #
        # We try removing subsets of the currently retained spans.
        #
        # If removing a subset keeps the EPUB BAD, those spans are not
        # necessary and we permanently remove them.
        #
        # If removing a subset makes it GOOD, at least one span in that
        # subset is necessary, so we keep them and subdivide further.
        # --------------------------------------------------------------

        log()
        log("=" * 72)
        log("BISECTING KOBO SPANS")
        log("=" * 72)

        log(
            "Goal: find the smallest set of Kobo spans that must be "
            "removed to make the EPUB GOOD."
        )

        granularity = 2

        while remaining:

            # The spans in `remaining` are currently NOT removed.
            #
            # Try deleting chunks from them.
            if len(remaining) == 1:
                granularity = 1
            else:
                granularity = min(
                    granularity,
                    len(remaining),
                )

            groups = self.split_indexes(
                remaining,
                granularity,
            )

            made_progress = False

            for group_number, group in enumerate(
                groups,
                start=1,
            ):

                log()
                log(
                    f"[KOBO TEST] remove group "
                    f"{group_number}/{len(groups)} "
                    f"({len(group)} spans)"
                )

                test_removed = (
                    removed
                    | set(group)
                )

                result = self.test_kobo_selection(
                    normalized_source_dir,
                    target_path,
                    original_data,
                    spans,
                    test_removed,
                    (
                        f"kobo-delete-"
                        f"{len(group)}"
                    ),
                )

                if result.bad:

                    # Great: these spans can be removed without fixing
                    # the bug. Therefore they are unnecessary.
                    removed.update(group)

                    remaining = [
                        index
                        for index in remaining
                        if index not in group
                    ]

                    made_progress = True

                    log(
                        f"    ACCEPT: removed "
                        f"{len(group)} Kobo spans"
                    )

                    break

                else:

                    log(
                        "    REJECT: at least one span in "
                        "this group is required"
                    )

            if made_progress:

                if not remaining:
                    break

                # Try the same granularity again with the smaller set.
                granularity = min(
                    granularity,
                    len(remaining),
                )

                continue

            # No group could be removed as a whole.
            #
            # Increase granularity, meaning smaller groups.
            if granularity < len(remaining):

                granularity = min(
                    len(remaining),
                    granularity * 2,
                )

                continue

            # We are already testing individual spans.
            # None can be removed individually.
            break

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # The above ddmin finds a 1-minimal set with respect to removing
        # individual spans, but do a final individual pass to make sure
        # no currently removed span can actually be restored.
        #
        # This is useful because interactions between removals can make
        # the first pass non-obvious.
        # --------------------------------------------------------------

        log()
        log("=" * 72)
        log("FINAL SINGLE-SPAN MINIMIZATION PASS")
        log("=" * 72)

        changed = True

        while changed:

            changed = False

            for index in list(
                sorted(removed)
            ):

                candidate_removed = (
                    removed
                    - {index}
                )

                log()
                log(
                    f"[FINAL TEST] restore Kobo span "
                    f"{index + 1}/{len(spans)}"
                )

                span = spans[index]

                if span.kobo_id:
                    log(
                        f"    id={span.kobo_id}"
                    )

                result = self.test_kobo_selection(
                    normalized_source_dir,
                    target_path,
                    original_data,
                    spans,
                    candidate_removed,
                    "kobo-restore-one",
                )

                if result.bad:

                    # It is safe to restore this span.
                    removed.remove(index)

                    changed = True

                    log(
                        "    RESTORE: span is not required "
                        "to be removed"
                    )

                else:

                    log(
                        "    KEEP REMOVED: span is required"
                    )

        final_data = remove_kobo_spans(
            original_data,
            spans,
            removed,
        )

        return (
            final_data,
            spans,
            removed,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Main cleaning operation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def clean(
        self,
        target_path: Optional[Path],
    ) -> None:

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Create normalized working EPUB.
        # --------------------------------------------------------------

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
            prefix="epub-cleaner-normalized-"
        ) as td:

            normalized_dir = (
                Path(td)
                / "normalized"
            )

            changed_files = (
                normalize_kobo_namespaces_in_directory(
                    self.source_dir,
                    normalized_dir,
                )
            )

            log()
            log("=" * 72)
            log("KOBO NAMESPACE NORMALIZATION")
            log("=" * 72)

            log(
                f"HTML/XHTML files changed: "
                f"{changed_files}"
            )

            # ----------------------------------------------------------
            # Automatic file discovery, if needed.
            #
            # IMPORTANT:
            #
            # The file isolation is performed on the NORMALIZED EPUB.
            # Therefore we first remove the redundant Kobo namespace
            # everywhere, then determine which HTML file is still
            # sufficient to trigger the problem.
            # ----------------------------------------------------------

            if target_path is None:

                html_paths = list_html_files(
                    normalized_dir
                )

                target_path = (
                    self.identify_problematic_file(
                        html_paths
                    )
                )

                if target_path is None:

                    die(
                        "No individual HTML/XHTML file was sufficient "
                        "to reproduce the problem after Kobo namespace "
                        "normalization."
                    )

            else:

                target_path = Path(
                    str(target_path)
                )

                if target_path.is_absolute():

                    die(
                        "--html-path must be relative to "
                        "the EPUB root."
                    )

                target_path = Path(
                    str(target_path).lstrip("./")
                )

                target_file = (
                    normalized_dir
                    / target_path
                )

                if not target_file.is_file():

                    die(
                        f"Target HTML/XHTML does not exist: "
                        f"{target_path}"
                    )

            # ----------------------------------------------------------
            # Minimize Kobo spans.
            # ----------------------------------------------------------

            (
                final_data,
                spans,
                removed,
            ) = self.minimize_kobo_spans(
                normalized_dir,
                target_path,
            )

            # ----------------------------------------------------------
            # Write final EPUB.
            #
            # Everything is copied from the normalized EPUB, with only
            # target_path replaced by the minimized XHTML.
            # ----------------------------------------------------------

            final_path = (
                self.output_dir
                / "FINAL-minimized.epub"
            )

            make_epub_with_one_replacement(
                normalized_dir,
                target_path,
                final_data,
                final_path,
            )

            # ----------------------------------------------------------
            # Report.
            # ----------------------------------------------------------

            log()
            log("=" * 72)
            log("FINAL RESULT")
            log("=" * 72)

            log(
                f"Target XHTML:       {target_path}"
            )

            log(
                f"Kobo spans found:   {len(spans)}"
            )

            log(
                f"Kobo spans removed: {len(removed)}"
            )

            log(
                f"Kobo spans kept:    "
                f"{len(spans) - len(removed)}"
            )

            log()

            if removed:

                log(
                    "Removed Kobo spans:"
                )

                for index in sorted(removed):

                    span = spans[index]

                    if span.kobo_id:

                        log(
                            f"  {index + 1:4d}: "
                            f"{span.kobo_id}"
                        )

                    else:

                        log(
                            f"  {index + 1:4d}: "
                            f"(no id)"
                        )

            else:

                log(
                    "No Kobo spans needed to be removed."
                )

            log()
            log(
                f"FINAL EPUB:"
            )
            log(
                f"  {final_path.resolve()}"
            )

            log()
            log(
                f"Total benchmark tests: "
                f"{self.test_number}"
            )

# ============================================================================
# Command line
# ============================================================================

def main() -> None:

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=(
            "Second-stage EPUB cleaner: normalize Kobo span namespaces "
            "and minimize the specific Kobo spans responsible for an "
            "Okular CPU problem."
        )
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "input",
        type=Path,
        help=(
            "Broken .epub file or unpacked EPUB directory"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--html-path",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Specific HTML/XHTML file to minimize, relative to the "
            "EPUB root. If omitted, automatically isolate the "
            "problematic HTML/XHTML file."
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--epub-reader",
        default="okular",
        help=(
            "EPUB reader command (default: okular)"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(
            "epub-minimizer-tests"
        ),
        help=(
            "Directory for test files and final EPUB "
            "(default: epub-minimizer-tests)"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--timeout",
        type=float,
        default=5.0,
        help=(
            "Maximum seconds to wait for CPU to become idle "
            "(default: 5)"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--interval",
        type=float,
        default=0.05,
        help=(
            "CPU sampling interval in seconds "
            "(default: 0.05)"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--idle-threshold",
        type=float,
        default=5.0,
        help=(
            "CPU percentage regarded as idle "
            "(default: 5)"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--idle-samples",
        type=int,
        default=3,
        help=(
            "Consecutive idle samples required for GOOD "
            "(default: 3)"
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--keep-tests",
        action="store_true",
        help=(
            "Keep intermediate test EPUBs instead of deleting them."
        ),
    )

    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-tests",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Maximum number of benchmark tests."
        ),
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.timeout <= 0:
        die(
            "--timeout must be greater than zero"
        )

    if args.interval <= 0:
        die(
            "--interval must be greater than zero"
        )

    if args.idle_samples <= 0:
        die(
            "--idle-samples must be greater than zero"
        )

    if args.idle_threshold < 0:
        die(
            "--idle-threshold cannot be negative"
        )

    if (
        args.max_tests is not None
        and args.max_tests <= 0
    ):
        die(
            "--max-tests must be greater than zero"
        )

    input_path = args.input.resolve()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Prepare source EPUB directory.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
        prefix="epub-cleaner-source-"
    ) as td:

        source_temp = Path(td)

        if input_path.is_dir():

            validate_epub_dir(
                input_path
            )

            source_dir = (
                source_temp
                / "epub"
            )

            copy_epub_directory(
                input_path,
                source_dir,
            )

        elif input_path.is_file():

            if input_path.suffix.lower() != ".epub":

                die(
                    f"Input file is not an EPUB: "
                    f"{input_path}"
                )

            source_dir = (
                source_temp
                / "epub"
            )

            unpack_epub(
                input_path,
                source_dir,
            )

        else:

            die(
                f"Input does not exist: "
                f"{input_path}"
            )

        # ----------------------------------------------------------------
        # Validate HTML files.
        # ----------------------------------------------------------------

        html_paths = list_html_files(
            source_dir
        )

        if not html_paths:

            die(
                "No HTML/XHTML files found in EPUB."
            )

        # ----------------------------------------------------------------
        # Parse reader command.
        # ----------------------------------------------------------------

        reader_command = shlex.split(
            args.epub_reader
        )

        if not reader_command:

            die(
                "--epub-reader cannot be empty"
            )

        # ----------------------------------------------------------------
        # Create cleaner.
        # ----------------------------------------------------------------

        cleaner = EPUBCleaner(
            source_dir=source_dir,
            output_dir=args.output_dir.resolve(),
            reader_command=reader_command,
            timeout=args.timeout,
            interval=args.interval,
            idle_threshold=args.idle_threshold,
            idle_samples=args.idle_samples,
            keep_tests=args.keep_tests,
            max_tests=args.max_tests,
        )

        log()
        log("=" * 72)
        log("EPUB CLEANER")
        log("=" * 72)

        log(
            f"Input:            {input_path}"
        )

        log(
            f"HTML/XHTML files: {len(html_paths)}"
        )

        log(
            f"Reader:           {' '.join(reader_command)}"
        )

        log(
            f"Timeout:          {args.timeout:.2f}s"
        )

        log(
            f"CPU interval:     {args.interval:.3f}s"
        )

        log(
            f"Idle threshold:   {args.idle_threshold:.1f}%"
        )

        log(
            f"Idle samples:     {args.idle_samples}"
        )

        log()

        # ----------------------------------------------------------------
        # Clean.
        # ----------------------------------------------------------------

        cleaner.clean(
            args.html_path
        )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### What this version should give you

The key difference is that the final XHTML is **not generated by an XML parser**. If the normalized input contains:

``` xml
<html>
   <body>
      <div>
         <p class="Register"><span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1173.1">– Kanalbau ...</span></p>
```

the cleaner will continue to use ordinary:

``` xml
<html>
<body>
<div>
<p>
```

and will not turn it into `html:html`, `html:body`, etc.

When it removes a Kobo span, it removes only the wrapper:

``` diff
- <span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1173.1">– Kanalbau und -erhaltung durch 131f., 205f.</span>
+ – Kanalbau und -erhaltung durch 131f., 205f.
```

So the actual final diff should be much more informative.

### One important thing to watch

The script deliberately tests this intermediate state first:

``` text
original EPUB
     ↓
remove xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
     ↓
NORMALIZED EPUB
     ↓
benchmark
```

If that alone makes Okular GOOD, you'll get:

``` text
IMPORTANT: normalized EPUB is already GOOD.
The namespace normalization itself fixed the problem.
```

That would mean **none of the Kobo spans need to be removed**.

If it is still BAD, it proceeds to the actual span minimization and eventually reports something like:

``` text
Kobo spans found:   1179
Kobo spans removed: 7
Kobo spans kept:    1172

Removed Kobo spans:
   381: kobo.381.1
   382: kobo.382.1
   383: kobo.383.1
   417: kobo.417.1
   ...
```

That is the interesting result we're after.

And because the normalized EPUB is used as the baseline, the final comparison should now be close to:

``` bash
diff -u0 \
  epub-contents-normalized/OEBPS/appendix-001.xhtml \
  epub-contents-good/OEBPS/appendix-001.xhtml
```

rather than the enormous `ElementTree` serialization diff from the previous run.

Yes — **Tree-sitter is a much better approach here**. The `Kobo spans found: 0` result is a bug in my textual scanner, and I would not try to patch that scanner further.

Your reasoning is exactly right: we want a **CST parser** that understands the XHTML structure but gives us the **original byte offsets**. Then the cleaner can make surgical edits:

``` text
original XHTML
     │
     ├── Tree-sitter parses it
     │
     ├── locate <span class="koboSpan" ...>...</span>
     │
     ├── obtain exact byte offsets of opening/closing tags
     │
     └── delete ONLY those bytes
```

That gives us the best of both worlds:

- proper XHTML/HTML parsing
- no `ElementTree` namespace rewriting
- no formatting changes
- no `html:` prefixes
- no guessing with regex about nested elements
- exact byte-level modifications

### One other change I'd make

I would **not normalize the namespace by doing a global replacement on the entire XHTML anymore**.

Instead, Tree-sitter should identify the actual Kobo `<span>` elements and we can remove the `xmlns="..."` attribute from **those start tags only**.

So the first transformation becomes:

``` xml
<span xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1173.1">
```

→

``` xml
<span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1173.1">
```

while everything else is byte-identical.

Then we benchmark that normalized EPUB.

If it's still BAD, we proceed to the much more interesting experiment:

``` text
1179 Kobo spans
       │
       ├── remove spans 1–590 → BAD/GOOD?
       ├── remove spans 591–1179 → BAD/GOOD?
       │
       └── recursively narrow down
                  ↓
             exact culprit(s)
```

And when removing a Kobo span, I agree with your intended semantics: **remove the `<span>` wrapper but preserve its contents**:

``` xml
<span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.123.1">some text</span>
```

becomes:

``` xml
some text
```

rather than deleting `some text`.

### The resulting diff should be extremely useful

Ideally we'll eventually get something like:

``` diff
 <p class="Register">
-    <span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.417.1">Akkad</span>
+    Akkad
 </p>
```

and perhaps only a handful of such changes.

Even better, the script can report:

``` text
Kobo spans found:   1179
Kobo spans removed:    3

Required removals:

    #417   kobo.417.1
    #418   kobo.418.1
    #419   kobo.419.1
```

That would give us a concrete hypothesis about what is broken in the EPUB rather than merely producing a minimized document.

**So yes: I would replace the regex-based XHTML manipulation with Tree-sitter rather than fixing the current scanner.** The next `epub_cleaner.py` should use `tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-html`, retain exact source byte offsets, and make all modifications by applying byte-range edits to the original XHTML.

## Response:

9/11/2026, 7:47:19 AM

Yes 😄 — that is much simpler, and I had the normalization scope wrong.

The intended pipeline is:

1.  **Parse every XHTML/HTML file with Tree-sitter.**
2.  **Normalize namespaces structurally:**
    - Keep `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"` on the **root `<html>` element**.
    - Remove that `xmlns` attribute from **every descendant element**.
    - Do not otherwise reformat or serialize anything.
    - In particular, preserve whitespace, attributes, text, line endings, etc. byte-for-byte.
3.  Create a normalized EPUB and benchmark it.
4.  Locate the problematic XHTML file if `--html-path` wasn't supplied.
5.  Parse that file again with Tree-sitter and identify actual `<span class="... koboSpan ...">` elements.
6.  Bisect the Kobo spans using **byte offsets**, removing only their opening and closing tags while leaving their contents untouched.
7.  Find a **1-minimal** set of Kobo spans whose removal makes the EPUB load quickly.
8.  Produce the final EPUB plus a precise report/diff of what changed.

So, for example:

``` xml
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
  <body>
    <div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
      <p xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
        <span xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" class="koboSpan">
          text
        </span>
      </p>
    </div>
  </body>
</html>
```

becomes:

``` xml
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
  <body>
    <div>
      <p>
        <span class="koboSpan">
          text
        </span>
      </p>
    </div>
  </body>
</html>
```

**and absolutely nothing else gets reserialized.**

Then, for the Kobo minimization, if we have:

``` xml
<span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1.1">foo</span>
<span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1.2">bar</span>
<span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1.3">baz</span>
```

the minimizer removes only:

``` text
<span ...>
</span>
```

for selected spans, resulting in e.g.:

``` xml
foo
<span class="koboSpan" id="kobo.1.2">bar</span>
baz
```

The actual text and every byte outside those tag ranges stays untouched.

One important distinction: I'll make the namespace cleanup apply to **all descendant elements**, not merely Kobo spans. Tree-sitter will tell us which element is the root `<html>` element, so the cleaner can preserve its namespace and remove the redundant descendant declarations safely.
